sources.observed: StreamableHttpService implements tower_service::Service<http::Request<RequestBody>>; its HTTP request path later propagates HTTP request Parts into MCP RequestContext extensions before dispatch.
The released official example constructs StreamableHttpService and mounts it with axum::Router::new().nest_service("/mcp", service) before axum::serve.

slice.bounded_search_result: A bounded repository search found no dedicated rmcp bearer/authentication middleware abstraction in the inspected Streamable HTTP integration surface. This is an absence-within-tested-scope finding, not a repository-wide proof of nonexistence.
slice.finding: The source-qualified trust boundary is application-owned HTTP middleware outside rmcp: authenticate the inbound HTTP request before forwarding to StreamableHttpService; on success insert a server-authenticated Principal (or equivalent identity object) into http::Request::extensions_mut(); on failure return an HTTP auth error without invoking the inner MCP service. Because the released rmcp service is a Tower Service<Request<_>> and the official example mounts it inside an Axum Router, this wrapper can be composed before rmcp dispatch without changing rmcp internals. rmcp then carries the resulting http::request::Parts into RequestContext extensions, where the tool path can read Parts and then parts.extensions for that Principal. Client `_meta` remains non-authoritative for identity.
minimal_application_owned_contract: Authentication runs before inner StreamableHttpService.call/dispatch and fails closed.
Principal is derived only from trusted server-side authentication state, never from MCP client metadata.
Successful authentication inserts Principal into the inbound http::Request extensions before forwarding.
The inner rmcp service is invoked exactly once for an accepted HTTP request.
Tool/request code obtains http::request::Parts from RequestContext extensions and then reads Principal from parts.extensions; missing Principal is an authorization failure.
Continuation tokens such as RequestStateCodec bind associated data to this authenticated Principal, not a client-asserted identifier.
not_proven: No concrete credential verifier or identity provider is supplied by rmcp in this tested slice.
This does not prove OAuth/JWT/API-key correctness, key rotation, revocation, or transport confidentiality.
This does not solve persistent task create-or-get, restart redrive, or external-effect idempotency/fencing.
